title: Sequence-sensitive hosted endpoint PRD + runtime-aware rollout playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a product requirements document and step-by-step launch checklist for a new hosted API packaging approach that is aware of sequence characteristics (context length, KV cache re-use, prefix locality) and automatically selects endpoint bundling, caching and fallback profiles for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank workloads. This PRD covers behavior, acceptance criteria, runtime constraints, rollout plan, and observability requirements for a staged cutover into Hosted API lane bundles.
background: Many customers run multi-modal flows that mix long chat histories, short completions, dense embedding requests and periodic rerank batches. Current single-surface endpoints force customers to choose between latency and cost or to implement brittle client-side routing. The platform can provide a unified hosted experience by exposing runtime-aware bundled endpoints that optimize batching, KV cache policies and model variants based on per-request sequence signals.
goals: Provide a single hosted API bundle that routes requests to runtime-optimized serving profiles without changes to existing SDKs
Reduce median token cost for mixed workloads by 25% for customers with >50% sequence-locality in chat traffic
Maintain P95 latency SLO for interactive chat under standard tier and document compliance for Dedicated/Private users
Deliver a safe, observable canary + automated rollback cutover procedure
success_metrics: Cost reduction: -25% token cost for target workloads as measured by baseline vs 30d after cutover
Latency: P95 end-to-end (client->response-first-byte) <= 450ms for short-chat (<=512 tokens) and <= 1200ms for long-chat scenarios in hosted-standard tier
Quality guardrails: No regression >2% absolute on primary NLU eval sets (chat coherence) and rerank NDCG drop <=1.5%
Reliability: error rate increase <=0.5 percentage points during rollout
Adoption: 20% of new hosted API customers auto-assigned to sequence-aware bundles within 90 days
in_scope: Design API contract changes (backwards compatible headers/options) to enable runtime hints such as context_length_hint and use_cache_preference
Server-side selection of bundle profiles (e.g., chat-optimized, embed-optimized, rerank-batch) with automatic fallback to stable variants
KV cache eviction and prefix caching policies exposed as configurable defaults per tenant
Console observability panels and cost/latency breakdown per bundle
Canary + gradual rollout tooling and automatic rollback triggers based on telemetry
out_of_scope: Major SDK breaking changes or new client-side routing responsibilities
On-prem private deployment packaging beyond configuration knobs (Private customers will receive config template only)
Changes to user-facing model catalog naming conventions
requirements: Backward-compatible header 'X-Redwood-Sequence-Hint' accepted and optional; default behavior unchanged if not provided
Server must inspect sequence hints and request metadata to select: batching profile, model quantization profile, and fallback policy
Support chat, completions, embeddings, rerank in same bundle API surface with per-request profile decision
Per-tenant override: allow customers to pin to 'cost-optimized' or 'latency-optimized' profiles
Runtime must expose per-request routing reason in response headers for debugging (e.g., 'X-RW-Bundle-Decision: chat-optimized')
Ensure KV cache reuse across tokens for same conversation id; default TTL 30 minutes unless tenant overrides
api_surface_changes: Add optional request header X-Redwood-Sequence-Hint: values {short, medium, long, streaming} or integer token estimate
Add optional tenant-level profile config via Console: profile=latency|cost|balanced
Return header X-RW-Bundle-Decision with selected profile and model variant
No change to existing top-level endpoints path (POST /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank) to preserve client code
runtime_constraints: Support continuous batching with max batch latency 50ms for short requests under typical load
KV cache must be addressable by conversation id and support prefix-pin for long-context retrievals
Model fallback chain must be limited to two steps (primary -> fallback) to bound latency degradation
Memory and GPU allocation heuristics should prioritize latency SLO for 'latency' profiles and density for 'cost' profiles
security_and_privacy: All tenant overrides stored encrypted with KMS and audited
Sequence hints must not be used to infer or expose PII; ensure we do not log full chat history in routing logs
Security review required for tenant-level profile feature (scope: KMS integration and audit log retention changes)
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests: routing decision header present and matches expected profile for synthetic scenarios (short/long/mixed)
Performance tests: meet latency and cost success metrics under standard test traffic patterns
Quality tests: eval harness shows no regression above stated thresholds for chat NLU and rerank metrics
Failover tests: simulate primary model OOM and confirm automatic fallback within configured chain without loss of data
Security: tenant override UI flows require admin role and are recorded in audit logs
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha on staging with e2e tests and synthetic traffic for 2 weeks. Phase 1: Beta customers (opt-in) for 4 weeks with telemetry monitoring and weekly review. Phase 2: Automatic assignment for low-risk tenants (traffic <500 rps) with 10% daily ramp. Phase 3: Full rollout with monitored cutover and 48h stabilization window. Automated rollback triggers include: +0.5% error rate, P95 latency increase beyond thresholds, quality regression alerts from eval harness.
canary_and_cutover_checks: Pre-cutover health: zero critical alerts in 72h for target cluster
Smoke test: end-to-end short chat scenario success (functional assertions) in <2s
Canary traffic: initial 1% traffic slice with 30m observation window
Automated guardrails: if any SLA or quality guard fires, rollback to previous routing behavior for affected tenants
observability_and_telemetry: New console panels: Bundle decision distribution, cost-per-token by bundle, P95 latency by bundle, error rate by bundle
Per-tenant telemetry retention 90d for bundle decisions and routing traces
Eval-driven quality alerts integrated: periodic synthetic prompt set runs with alert thresholds tied to rollout automation
Expose sample traces and synthetic prompt results to solutions-eng for customer investigations
launch_checklist_prelaunch: Docs: update API docs and SDK changelog with header usage and behavior
Console: add tenant profile UI and RBAC gating for overrides
Infra: ensure autoscaling policies for new bundle profiles are defined and tested
Telemetry: dashboards created and alert thresholds configured
Security: KMS audit for tenant overrides completed
QA: integration + performance test runs green on staging
launch_checklist_launch: Enable feature flag for sequence-aware bundles on control plane for staging clusters
Kick off canary routing at 1% per plan and monitor 60m windows
Confirm no quality regressions on eval harness during canary
Gradually increase traffic per plan and confirm console metrics match expectations
Communicate to Beta customers with runbook and support contact
launch_checklist_postlaunch: Daily review for first 7 days with cross-functional rotations (PM/Eng/SE/SRE)
Collect customer feedback and enable opt-out for early adopters
Measure cost and latency deltas and prepare executive report at 30d
Finalize runbook edits and certify feature for GA
Schedule follow-up scope for Dedicated/Private packaging based on uptake and feedback
dependencies: ENG-12045: KV cache TTL per-tenant control
PM-612345: hosted endpoint SLA tier definitions
risks: Hidden quality regressions for long-tail prompts not covered by eval sets
Unexpected cost increases for tenants with highly bursty short requests
Operational complexity in debugging routing decisions across many variants
Tenant confusion if automatic routing differs from documented behavior
mitigations: Maintain an eval-matrix that covers long-tail prompt clusters and add synthetic fuzzing
Introduce conservative cost-safety caps and allow tenant opt-in for cost-optimized default
Return verbose routing headers and provide a debug mode with limited retention
Clear documentation and gradual opt-in defaults; customer comms for changes
notes: This PRD focuses on the hosted API experience. Dedicated and Private offerings will be given configuration templates post-GA. Security review is marked required because tenant-level overrides change audit surface and KMS usage. Work with SRE to ensure rollback automation is battle-tested before expanding beyond Beta customers.
